messages:
maria: FYI planning a sparse-refresh for the edge GPU cohort in apac-west1 tonight 00:30-02:30 UTC. goal: rotate ~20% of nodes to pick up BMC/kernel fixes without causing a large KV-cache cold start spike.
kevin: +1. whats the rollout strategy? can we stagger at pod-affinity level to avoid hitting trailing-latency SLOs?
ashley: propose cohorts of 5 nodes, 10min stagger between cohorts, and prime kv-cache on warm nodes before draining. will run canary on a single tenant group first.
maria: exact plan: 1) canary cohort (2 nodes) 00:30-00:40, 2) gradual cohorts (5 nodes) 00:45 onwards with 10m offset, 3) backfill jobs to re-seed KV caches. 4) fallback: immediate stop + rollback to previous routing if >3% P90 increase.
jordan: tagging @oncall for overlap — I'm oncall then. can we add a safe window for long-running jobs? some customers have midnight batch jobs.
kevin: good call. I've pulled tenant-priority map — we'll mark high-priority tenants as immune during their schedule windows. snippet: `./tools/tenantctl set-evacuation-exempt --tenant-id=TENANT123`
maria: ops-bot will run the cohort commands; I'll drop the runbook link once staged. ops-bot: scheduled job queued for 2026-03-21T00:30:00Z.
ops-bot: preflight checks: cluster health OK, free GPU capacity 24%, cross-region backfill capacity available in us-east1.
ashley: cost ask: using cross-region backfill increases egress costs for KV fetches. rough estimate +$120/hr if we keep backfill for full window. approve?
kevin: approve up to $150/hr for the maintenance window; prefer to keep backfill active only while cohort drains are happening.
jordan: monitoring hooks: add synthetic latency probe on the hot-path and token-generation p95 alert at +30s. runbook -> step 4 has rollback commands.
maria: copy. will set alerts and a short blameless note for customers if we hit fallback. also i'll run a quick canary load: `curl -s -XPOST https://api.redwood.internal/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"prime"}'`
kevin: one more: if netlink queue spikes during BMC cycle we might see connection drops. add a 60s grace to kubelet before evict. use `kubectl drain --grace-period=60 --ignore-daemonsets`.
ashley: adding a small KV pre-warm: `python tools/kv_warm.py --cohort-id=c1 --rate=200/s` — will start 10m before cohort drain.
maria: timeline posted in ops channel and customer-facing advisory drafted for affected tenants. will update if anything changes. :thumbsup:
jordan: I'll be watching and will post rolling status updates. ping me if P95 > threshold. :eyes:
kevin: ack. good luck.
ops-bot: maintenance started (canary). logs: `canary-cohort=2 nodes; drain_ok=2/2; kv_warm=started`
maria: canary looks clean — no latency blips. proceeding with cohort 1.
kevin: confirming cohort 1 drain complete. freeing up 5 nodes. backfill running at reduced rate to limit egress.
ashley: cost so far ~ $40 (partial backfill) — within budget.
ops-bot: maintenance complete for scheduled window. summary: 22% pool rotated, canary ok, no SLO violations.
maria: huge thanks team. will close postmortem and update maintenance calendar.
